entities.summary: David Sloane Stanley was a Union Army general during the American Civil War. Stanley took part in the Second Battle of Corinth and the Battle of Stones River as a division commander. He was later made a corps commander under William Tecumseh Sherman and sent to Tennessee to oppose John Bell Hood's Army of Tennessee. At a critical moment in the Battle of Franklin, he saved part of George D. Wagner’s division from destruction, earning America's highest military decoration, the Medal of Honor. Later he explored the Yellowstone River, and his favorable reports encouraged settlement of this region.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: David S. Stanley's actions at the Battle of Franklin saved part of George D. Wagner’s division from destruction, earning him the Medal of Honor. This heroic act had a significant regional impact, as it contributed to the Union victory in the Battle of Franklin and ultimately led to the defeat of the Confederate Army.
